transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Well, I'm mostly here because my wife and I have been disagreeing about something, and I guess she wanted me to talk to someone. 

For the past year or so, she's been having these late meetings, and I've noticed these little changes in her work messages. She says it's just normal office stuff. But... when you actually pay attention, they line up too precisely to just feel accidental. It's like there’s a private signal in them, you know? Like they're meant to tell me something that she just won’t say directly to me. She thinks I'm reading into things, so, that's what brings me in.
Besides these suspicions about the messages, have you noticed anything else unusual—like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or seeing things that aren't there?

No, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or... see things that aren't there. My hearing and vision are perfectly fine. 

It's really just, well, what I was telling you about. The messages and the timing of those late meetings. Everything else is completely normal. I'm just looking at the actual texts and emails she gets, I'm not... making things up out of thin air. So, no, nothing like hearing voices.

Aside from your wife, do you find yourself generally suspicious or distrustful of other people in your life—like coworkers, friends, or family—wondering if they might be hiding things or trying to deceive you?

No, not really. I mean, I get along fine with the professors I work with, and the students are just... students. I don't have any issues with my friends or my brother, either. 

It's just this one specific thing with my wife. I don't walk around thinking everyone is out to get me or lying to me. It's really just those messages and the meetings. Everything else in my life, and everyone else, is completely fine.

Over this past year, have you noticed any changes in how well you're able to concentrate on your work, keep up with your usual responsibilities, or engage with colleagues and friends the way you used to?

No, not really. I mean, my work hasn't suffered at all. I still show up for all my teaching sections, and I keep up with my data analysis just fine. And socially, things are the same. I still ride my bike, I meet up with my friends for chess... everything there is normal. 

The main place this actually causes any trouble is just at home, when my wife and I get stuck arguing about what her work schedule really means. But as far as my usual responsibilities or my focus at work, no, there haven't been any changes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, fixed, non-bizarre delusion of infidelity (jealous type) focused exclusively on his wife, persisting for approximately one year. He denies hallucinations, other forms of paranoia, or mood symptoms, and maintains full occupational and social functioning outside of the marital conflict generated by the delusion. This pattern—an isolated, encapsulated delusional belief without hallucinations, disorganized thought, negative symptoms, or broader impairment—is classic for Delusional Disorder, Jealous Type (F22.0). Schizophrenia (F20.0) is excluded due to absence of hallucinations, disorganization, or functional decline. Paranoid personality disorder (F60.0) is excluded because suspicion is not pervasive across relationships but limited to a specific delusional belief about his wife.
